description: HLS origin control plane — Node HTTP server that lists active streams by scanning the shared hls-data volume for stream.m3u8 playlists.

buildHints.whenToUse: Any project that needs an HLS live-streaming origin: self-hosted Twitch-style ingest, live event broadcasting, video CDN origin, or multi-stream monitoring dashboards. Use when you need a segmented .m3u8 playlist that browsers can pull directly.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `docker compose up -d` — nginx starts on port {{nginxPort}}, the ffmpeg container stays idle waiting for streams.
Run `pnpm dev` to start the control plane on port {{port}}. GET /health confirms the server and volume config. GET /streams lists active HLS streams.
Run `./start-stream.sh testsrc demo` to transcode a synthetic test pattern — segments appear in the shared hls-data volume immediately.
Open `http://localhost:{{nginxPort}}/hls/demo/stream.m3u8` in Safari or an hls.js player to confirm the live stream.
Extend `src/server.ts` to add per-stream start/stop endpoints, auth middleware, or webhook callbacks on stream-start/stream-end events.
gotchas: Segment duration is a latency/stability tradeoff — 2s segments give ~6s glass-to-glass latency with a 3-segment buffer; shorter segments reduce latency at the cost of more playlist churn and higher buffering risk on flaky networks.
Browsers require CORS on both the playlist AND every segment. The nginx.conf adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin to .m3u8 and .ts responses — removing either header breaks HLS.js.
Safari plays HLS natively; Chrome/Firefox need hls.js. Feature-detect with `video.canPlayType('application/vnd.apple.mpegurl')` — non-empty means native, otherwise bundle hls.js.
ffmpeg's `-hls_flags delete_segments` is mandatory for a rolling window — without it the origin fills disk with every 2s segment ever transcoded.
RTMP ingest is TCP port 1935, plaintext. Put nginx-rtmp or srtrelay in front for auth/TLS; the ffmpeg container here assumes a trusted ingest source.
libx264 in start-stream.sh is CPU-bound and single-stream. For production scale use h264_videotoolbox (macOS) or h264_nvenc (NVIDIA) by passing a custom FFMPEG_EXTRA_ARGS environment variable.
architectureNotes: nginx and ffmpeg share the hls-data named volume — ffmpeg writes .ts segments and .m3u8 playlists, nginx reads them with sendfile(). The Node server never touches media data.
The Node control plane is a management API only: it scans the hls-data volume for active playlists and exposes them over HTTP. Keep media delivery on nginx, not Node.
Each stream is a sub-directory of /var/www/hls/ — stream name maps directly to the URL path: /hls/<name>/stream.m3u8. This makes per-stream isolation trivial.

placeholders.description: Template variables {{port}}, {{nginxPort}}, {{serviceName}} are replaced at compose time. The /health and /streams routes are fully wired — add auth, per-stream lifecycle endpoints, or webhook hooks here.
